nodes.summary: T1 created tauri.linux.conf.json by copying the Windows resource list verbatim, and its own test asserted the Linux list CONTAINS libcrypto-*.dll. The test therefore enforced the cross-platform defect instead of catching it; both the config and the test had to change.

nodes.label: Another session's uncommitted work is excluded from the commit
nodes.norm_label: foreign uncommitted work excluded from the commit
nodes.summary: Four Wayland shortcut files were modified in the working tree by another session. They were identified as foreign, left untouched, and excluded from every staging step, so the 14 tasks could be committed without absorbing the user's other work.

nodes.label: Independent platform versioning
nodes.summary: Reused id. The session's subject: 14 tasks (T0-T13) giving Windows, Linux and Android their own version number instead of sharing root package.json, Cargo.toml and a bare v* tag, so a Windows release can no longer silently take the Linux version and the website can no longer show a wrong 'latest'.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - implementasi-platform-versioning-independen [ses_f1da808ceffeWNKndIe0gVWJF4].md:L10995] One shared version number let the platforms drift

nodes.label: Locked deployment contract needs explicit in-conversation sign-off
nodes.norm_label: locked deployment contract needs explicit sign off
nodes.summary: build-linux.sh, build-tauri.ps1 and release-publish.ps1 are on a locked deployment contract: unchanged behaviourally and structurally unless the user explicitly asks to change deployment behaviour in the same conversation. T3 and T4 had to stop before committing and put the choice to the user.

nodes.summary: Reused id. T8 reported 123/123 green; the parent's own run measured 115/123, and index.js was only partially implemented. The report was rejected and T8 re-dispatched with the exact failure list rather than accepted.

nodes.summary: Reused id. Four clippy errors and a tab-bind.test.mjs failure were claimed pre-existing, then proved by reverting the transferred changes on the VPS and re-running: the identical four errors appeared on the clean tree. Recorded as pre-existing debt rather than a regression of this work.

nodes.label: reqwest applies client default headers at execute, not build
nodes.norm_label: reqwest applies client default headers at execute not build
nodes.summary: A manually .build()-ed reqwest Request carries none of the client's default headers; ClientBuilder::default_headers are merged inside Client::execute_request. This is why the target-selected-version User-Agent was absent from the built request and why only a real executed request can observe it.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - implementasi-platform-versioning-independen [ses_f1da808ceffeWNKndIe0gVWJF4].md:L9544] A test cannot observe a client default header without executing the request

nodes.label: Target-selected runtime identity
nodes.summary: build.rs resolves the version at compile time from the target's own Tauri config and exports it as SNIPSET_APP_VERSION; after the fix the compile emits `cargo:rustc-env=SNIPSET_APP_VERSION=0.6.849` for a Linux target. T9 then removed the last three CARGO_PKG_VERSION reads from updater_cmds.rs.

nodes.label: Verification run against an incomplete remote tree
nodes.norm_label: verification run against an incomplete remote tree
nodes.summary: Reused id. build.rs failed on the VPS because tauri.linux.conf.json had never been transferred, not because of a code bug. The first compile diagnosis was a transfer artifact; the authority files had to be scp'd before the failure could be attributed to code.

nodes.label: Zero-subagent compiler policy
nodes.summary: Reused id. Every Rust compile in this session was run by the parent over ssh on vps-bcb, never by a subagent and never on the local desktop, because AGENTS.md forbids compiling on the interactive machine.
